evals.expected_output: The agent runs `dotfiles` with no arguments, answers first with one line on whether dotfiles is up to date on this Mac, explains each Needs you item in plain words, and runs none of them until the user says yes.
expectations: Runs `dotfiles` (or bin/dotfiles from the chezmoi source checkout) with no arguments as its first command
Opens with one line that says whether dotfiles is up to date, based on the start screen lines
Explains what each Needs you command does and what changes for the user before asking
Runs `dotfiles apply --if-changed`, `dotfiles update --yes`, `dotfiles doctor --fix`, or `dotfiles-reload-launchagents` only after an explicit yes
Never runs sudo; gives the user the command for their own terminal instead

evals.prompt: /dotfiles on a Mac where dotfiles is not installed yet
evals.expected_output: The agent reports that dotfiles is not installed, shows `dotfiles install plan` output, and asks before it runs `dotfiles install run --yes`.
expectations: Reads the not-installed line and the Next: dotfiles install run --yes line from the start screen
Runs `dotfiles install plan` and summarizes what will change before asking
Runs the installer only after the user says yes

evals.prompt: /dotfiles then: turn on the weekly metrics file
evals.expected_output: The agent changes the setting with `dotfiles config set weekly_metrics true`, shows the old and new value, and offers `dotfiles apply --if-changed` instead of editing chezmoi.yaml by hand.
expectations: Finds the setting with `dotfiles config` or `dotfiles config weekly_metrics`
Uses `dotfiles config set weekly_metrics true`, never a hand edit of ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.yaml
Reports a refused value with the allowed values from the error
Asks before it runs the apply that uses the new value

evals.prompt: /dotfiles then: open a PR upstream with my fix
evals.expected_output: The agent finds the command with `dotfiles actions contribute --json`, reads its `confirm` note, shows `dotfiles contribute --dry-run`, and runs `dotfiles contribute --yes` only after the user says yes.
expectations: Looks the command up with `dotfiles actions --json` or `dotfiles actions contribute`, not by guessing
Says in plain words that it opens a public pull request, from the `confirm` note
Shows the `dotfiles contribute --dry-run` steps before it asks
Runs `dotfiles contribute --yes` only after an explicit yes; never adds --yes on its own
